title: Anuttarāṣṭikā — The Supreme Eight
author: Abhinavagupta
text:
The Anuttarāṣṭikā is a compact hymn of eight verses by Abhinavagupta, from the classical period of Kashmir Shaivism (c. late tenth century). Its governing question is the tradition's most delicate: what is the method, when no method is enjoined? Contemplation, speech, conduct — none is prescribed as a means to be striven after, because the Supreme is not a result to be produced. The eight verses hold the paradox steady: there is practice, and there is no practice to be added from outside; the Real is already the condition of the one who seeks it.

Its juice: renounce the grammar of means and ends entirely. What remains — attention resting in what is — is itself the Supreme, and the hymn's restraint is its teaching: nothing is to be done to what is never absent.
